title: Procurement
goal: A practitioner can read the procurement artefact at a glance.

rubric.must: The named scenario is visibly identified and its primary subject is clearly shown.
The picture visibly uses the required standard diagram structure and connected elements.
A reader can visually follow the principal flow or relationship from beginning to end.
Key labels remain legible and attached to the correct visible elements.
Lines and symbols do not visually imply unintended connections.

ideal.notes: Drawn by `scripts/visual-eval/draw-idef0-target.mjs`, which draws all five IDEF0 cases from one kit so the set is one drawing repeated. An IDEF0 A0 function model of Procurement, drawn to FIPS PUB 183. Four function boxes — Approve requisition (1), Select supplier (2), Place purchase order (3), Match and pay invoice (4) — step down a diagonal staircase from upper left to lower right, each with its box number in the lower-right interior corner, and every box has at least one control and one output, as the standard requires. Every arrow occupies the edge its role requires: inputs enter the left edge, controls descend into the top, outputs leave the right, mechanisms rise into the bottom. Each label sits outside the box at the arrow's open end, and every boundary arrow carries its ICOM code (C1, I1, M1, O1 …, numbered along its own edge) where it meets the frame. The page carries the standard frame with a bottom title block of three cells: node, title and number. Where a boundary input has to cross mechanism arrows on its way to a later box, each crossing is drawn as a hop, so it cannot be misread as a junction — IDEF0 marks a real junction by merging arrows, never by touching them. Every label was checked against every other label, every box and the canvas edge: 0 overlaps.
